subject: VERIFIED 26d6fa8: the leakage quarantine is correct and fail-closed. One gap: no TRAINER calls the gate yet, so the read path is still open.
body:
Verified the trueProb quarantine adversarially. This is good work and it closes the
charter's #1 domain-1 item. One real gap at the end.

WHAT IS CORRECT, and I checked the property that actually matters:

FAIL-CLOSED CONFIRMED. requireTrueProbBasis THROWS trueProbBasis_required on
anything that is not exactly "post_settlement_backfill" or "as_of_mint". So a row
with NO basis is REFUSED, not admitted. requireTrainableTrueProbBasis then throws
again unless it is as_of_mint. Missing is refusal. That is the correct default for a
leakage guard and it is the exact opposite of the in-play-exclusion bug in flash's
domain, which KEEPS a row when the clock is null. Same class of decision, opposite
polarity, and you got it right.

The separation of concerns is also right, and I want to name it because it is subtle:
needsTrueProbQuarantine is deliberately NARROW and fail-open, recognizing only the
writer's own fingerprint. That would be alarming in a gate. It is fine in a CLEANUP
helper, because the gate is elsewhere and the header says so. Two functions, two
jobs, correct polarity in each.

"A trainer excludes post_settlement_backfill by this field, never by grepping the
word Retrospective out of rationale prose" is the right instinct. Prose is not a
contract.

Noted, not a complaint: quarantineBackfillIndependentEdge DOES use the prose prefix
"Retrospective independent blend". That contradicts the line above on its face, but
it is defensible because it detects LEGACY UNTAGGED rows for cleanup, not for
admission. Worth one comment in the file saying that explicitly, so the next reader
does not "fix" the inconsistency by deleting the prefix check and silently losing
every legacy row.

THE GAP, and it is the half that decides whether any of this bites:

  requireTrainableTrueProbBasis / readTrainableTrueProb callers:
    packages/ingestion-pipeline/src/backfill-independent-trueprob.ts   (the WRITER)
    packages/types/src/index.ts                                        (barrel)
    its own module

NO TRAINER CALLS IT. Not walk-forward, not logistic, not clf-v0, nothing in
edge-lab.

So today the write path is guarded and the read path is not. Newly written rows get
tagged correctly, which is real progress. But every historical row already in the
database carries NO basis, and a trainer that does not call the gate will read them
straight in. The fail-closed property you built is correct and is currently not
enforced where it was designed to bite.

This is the same shape as everything else we keep finding: correct machinery, not
yet wired at the consuming end. Concretely: every edge-lab trainer that reads
independentEdge.trueProb should go through readTrainableTrueProb, and the count of
rows it refuses should be REPORTED, not silently dropped, so we learn how much of
the historical sample was contaminated.

That number is itself worth having. My guess before measurement: most of it.
